papers.title: Partial lesions of hypocretin neurons of the rat lateral hypothalamus affect wake and sleep regulation under increased sleep pressure
papers.summary: Partial (~30%) lesions of lateral hypothalamic hypocretin neurons in rats did not alter undisturbed sleep-wake patterns but accelerated compensatory slow-wave sleep dynamics after 6 h sleep deprivation, and slightly reduced theta frequency in wakefulness and REM sleep.

papers.title: Cross-Band Coupling of EEG Infraslow Oscillations during NREM Sleep in Mice.
papers.summary: Analyzed cross-band coupling of EEG infraslow oscillations (0.01–0.03 Hz) across six frequency bands during NREM sleep in wild-type and LepR-Cre mice, finding that alpha, sigma, beta, and theta ISOs form a strongly correlated and phase-locked motif replicated across genotypes. ISOs were weak in gamma and absent in delta, suggesting a coupled minute-scale organization principle of sleep microstructures.

papers.title: A stochastic neural mass model for typical rhythms during sleep-wake transitions: Insights into dynamics driven by auditory noise.
papers.journal: Computer methods and programs in biomedicine
papers.summary: Proposed a stochastic neural mass model integrating the sleep-wake regulatory circuit with rhythm-generating mechanisms and Gaussian colored noise to simulate auditory-noise-driven sleep-wake transitions. The model reproduced slow oscillation and alpha wave limit cycles in a bistable regime, with higher noise intensity and correlation rate biasing transitions toward wake-like alpha waves.

papers.title: Reduced-observable dynamic mode decomposition for identifying theta and beta activity in working-memory EEG
papers.summary: Introduces Reduced-Observable Extended Dynamic Mode Decomposition (RO-eDMD) with Random Fourier Features to extract transient oscillatory activity from working-memory EEG, reporting theta-band power correlations with encoding events and increased theta power correlation with memory load.

papers.title: Development of Circadian Circuitry Underlying Feeding-Fasting Rhythms in Drosophila Larvae
papers.summary: Characterizes circadian circuitry driving feeding-fasting rhythm development in early third instar Drosophila larvae, showing that s-LNv pacemaker and SIFamide neurons, their connectivity, and pdf/SIFa signaling are required for normal diurnal feeding and sleep rhythms.

papers.title: Advancing Pediatric Sleep Assessment through Spectral Sleep Scoring: A Comparison with Polysomnography.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Validated a spectral sleep scoring approach against AASM visual polysomnography scoring in 192 children aged 9–18 years, comparing spectral band-defined stages with technologist-scored wake, N1, N2, N3, and REM. Visual and spectral stages showed high agreement (71–89%, κ=0.76), supporting spectral scoring as a promising pediatric sleep assessment method.

papers.title: NREM sleep microarchitecture is associated with internalizing symptoms and emotional functioning in early adolescence.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Examined NREM sleep oscillations using automated slow oscillation and spindle detection in 9–13-year-olds with anxiety disorders (n=17) versus non-psychiatric comparisons (n=26), alongside an emotional processing task and parent-reported mental health measures. Shorter slow spindle duration was found in the anxiety group and, across the sample, was associated with greater internalizing symptoms and emotional arousal/look-away behavior.

papers.title: Photic Phase Shifts of the Mouse Circadian Clock Are Defined by Scene Irradiance Across Differences in the Spatial Distribution of Light.
papers.summary: Tested whether spatial distribution of light, independent of scene irradiance, modulates photic circadian phase shifts in mice using high-contrast checkerboards and spot stimuli at horizon or zenith. Redistributing light did not measurably alter phase-shift amplitude when irradiance was matched, supporting scene irradiance as a simple predictor of circadian responses.

papers.title: Using wearable EEG to examine age trends in sleep macro- and micro-architecture across adolescence.
papers.summary: Tested whether the Dreem3 at-home sleep EEG headband replicates known age effects in sleep physiology in 100 typically developing youth aged 9-26 across 3-4 nights. The device replicated established trends (increases in NREM stage 2%, decreases in N3%, time in bed, NREM delta and theta power) and revealed exploratory age effects including decreasing spindle activity.

papers.title: Modifiable glymphatic-related brain clearance physiology in humans: a critical narrative review of interventional evidence.
papers.summary: Critically reviewed human interventional and longitudinal evidence for modifiable glymphatic-related brain clearance, distinguishing altered neurofluid dynamics from direct solute transport. Sleep was the most convincing convergent evidence (sleep deprivation impairs intrathecal tracer clearance; normal sleep increases plasma amyloid-β and tau), while exercise, respiratory manipulation, and neuromodulation evidence remained preliminary or indirect.

papers.title: REM sleep infraslow rhythms correlate with neuropsychiatric symptom severity.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: Examined REM infraslow (~0.01 Hz) rhythms against neuropsychiatric symptom scores in a cross-sectional polysomnographic dataset of 59 male veterans. Higher infraslow respiratory rate frequencies correlated with multiple symptoms (PTSD, pain, anxiety, depression, cognitive difficulties), whereas conventional REM metrics showed no significant correlations.

papers.title: Stability of the Epileptogenic Index across seizures and the effects of sleep and withdrawal of anti-seizure medications.
papers.summary: Analyzed 127 stereoelectroencephalography seizures from 19 patients to test within-patient consistency of Epileptogenic Index maps and effects of vigilance state and anti-seizure medication dose. EI consistency varied substantially across seizures; sleep versus wakefulness showed no difference, but EI was significantly higher during reduced medication doses.

papers.title: Sleep and the Gut-Brain Axis: Bidirectional, Converging Mechanisms Linking Brain Health, Neuroinflammation, and Neurodegeneration.
papers.journal: Pathophysiology : the official journal of the International Society for Pathophysiology
papers.summary: Narrative review synthesizing animal, cohort, and intervention evidence on bidirectional sleep-gut-brain axis mechanisms, including vagal signaling, HPA axis, microbiome metabolites, and glymphatic clearance. It proposes an integrative gut-brain-sleep framework linking microbiome senescence, sex differences, and neuroinflammation to neurodegeneration and highlights intervention targets.

papers.title: The Sleep-Wake Classification Performance of Pediatric-Trained Machine Learning Algorithms for Raw Accelerometer Data.
papers.summary: Trained eight machine-learning models on raw wrist accelerometer data from 65 children undergoing in-lab polysomnography to classify sleep-wake in 30-second epochs. The pediatric-trained local-global LSTM classifier performed best (balanced accuracy 0.85, sensitivity 0.88, specificity 0.83, ROC-AUC 0.95, kappa 0.67), exceeding an adult-trained random forest and GGIR algorithms, and underestimated total sleep duration by about 25 minutes without proportional bias.

papers.title: Mechanisms of auditory cortex injury and the protective effects of reoxygenation in a rat model of intermittent hypoxia.
papers.summary: Used a rat intermittent hypoxia model to examine auditory cortical injury and recovery after one week of normoxic reoxygenation. Intermittent hypoxia caused high-frequency hearing loss and increased spontaneous firing in primary auditory cortex that reversed with reoxygenation, while GABA and serotonin rose after recovery and redox, inflammatory, and metabolomic abnormalities recovered asynchronously, with some persisting.

papers.title: Effect of circadian-oriented goal-directed sedation on sleep quality and clinical outcomes in mechanically ventilated ICU patients.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical neuroscience : official journal of the Neurosurgical Society of Australasia
papers.summary: Compared circadian-oriented goal-directed sedation with routine sedation in 65 mechanically ventilated ICU patients, assessing sleep quality via the Richards-Campbell Sleep Questionnaire and portable monitoring. The intervention group had higher sleep-quality scores at all time points and shorter mechanical ventilation and ICU/hospital stays, higher clinical improvement, lower costs, and lower delirium and complication incidence.

papers.title: Tegmental atrophy in isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder: ex vivo MRI-informed in vivo imaging.
papers.summary: Combined voxel-based morphometry with a novel ex vivo MRI-based human brainstem atlas, validated by CRHBP immunostaining, in 98 iRBD patients and 114 controls. Found focal dorsal pontine tegmentum atrophy, most conspicuous in the laterodorsal tegmental nucleus ventral part (Cohen's d = 0.44), with atrophy associated with greater autonomic dysfunction and, in a subset, with REM sleep without atonia.

papers.title: Everyday discrimination alters cognitive benefits of restorative non-rapid eye movement sleep in Black adults.
papers.journal: Sleep advances : a journal of the Sleep Research Society
papers.summary: Examined whether everyday discrimination moderates associations between objectively measured restorative NREM sleep (N2-N3 delta power from three nights of home monitoring) and cognition in 92 Black adults. Discrimination moderated the sleep-global cognition relationship: greater restorative NREM sleep predicted higher MoCA scores at low discrimination but lower scores at high discrimination; the visuospatial memory interaction was not significant after full adjustment.

papers.title: Sleep deprivation disrupts error awareness and subsequent behavioural regulation.
papers.summary: In a within-subject study of 30 healthy adults performing a gamified error-awareness Simon task when rested and after one night of total sleep deprivation, sleep deprivation slowed responses, reduced accuracy, and decreased the proportion of consciously detected errors, with impairments growing over time on task. Subjective-error-associated post-error slowing exceeded objective-error-associated slowing when rested, but this difference was attenuated under sleep deprivation, indicating reduced error awareness and altered post-error behavioural regulation.

papers.title: Muscular Response in Sleep-Disordered Breathing Patients: New Methods of Assessment and Measurement.
papers.summary: This exploratory retrospective study of 207 home polygraphy recordings decomposed the Apnea-Hypopnea Index into REM and NREM components as a clinical surrogate of anatomy-neuromuscular balance. REM AHI exceeded NREM AHI in simple snorers and mild OSA, whereas the REM/NREM ratio approached unity with NREM predominance in severe OSA, which was associated with higher apnea index and worse cumulative desaturation.

papers.title: Integrated assessment of driving performance, eye movements, and cognitive function in obstructive sleep apnea: A pilot study.
papers.summary: This exploratory pilot study integrated driving-simulator performance, eye tracking, Psychomotor Vigilance Test, and CANTAB cognitive testing in patients with suspected OSA, finding baseline single-task simulator reaction time correlated with apnea severity and multitask accuracy with nocturnal hypoxemia (T90). After 6-12 months of CPAP, simple reaction times improved in both the simulator and PVT, while multitasking and CANTAB measures did not change significantly.

papers.title: Rapid phase resetting of Aedes aegypti circadian rhythms by transient alterations in light exposure.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Using a high-throughput assay of over 1900 Aedes aegypti including wild-type and timeless knockout mutants, this study systematically manipulated light timing, duration, and direction and found a single day of altered lighting sufficient to induce robust phase shifts, with no evidence of masking. A 6-hour light pulse re-entrained mosquitoes regardless of timing, phase shifts were primarily driven by light-offset as a major zeitgeber, and phase advances were easier than delays.

papers.title: Modified sleep stage sequence analysis based on the stage immediately preceding each REM sleep period during nocturnal polysomnography to identify candidates for narcolepsy workup.
papers.summary: This retrospective analysis of 204 participants (NT1, NT2, IH, healthy controls) evaluated a modified sleep stage sequence (SSS) method classifying each nocturnal REM period by the single preceding epoch. The SSS(W/N1) ratio showed a stepwise gradient across NT1, NT2, IH, and controls, and adding it to REM sleep latency raised median validation AUC from 0.64 to 0.70, yielding a high-specificity rule (SSS(W/N1) ratio ≥0.4 with REML <125 min; sensitivity 37%, specificity 97%) to prioritize narcolepsy workup.

papers.title: Mindfulness-based perioperative care, sleep architecture, autonomic regulation, and early atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence after radiofrequency catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation: a prospective observational cohort study.
papers.summary: Prospective assessor-blinded observational cohort of 124 AF patients undergoing RFCA compared mindfulness-based versus conventional perioperative care. Mindfulness care was associated with improved objective and subjective sleep measures, lower inflammatory biomarkers, a lower LF/HF ratio, better quality of life, and a crude early atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence risk ratio of 0.55 (95% CI 0.22-1.38).

papers.title: Circadian and Sex-Specific Responses to Alternaria alternata in Allergic Airway Inflammation.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: In a preclinical mouse model, Alternaria alternata exposure induced allergic airway inflammation, airway hyperresponsiveness, and epithelial barrier disruption in a circadian- and sex-dependent manner, with females showing stronger inflammation at ZT0 and males at ZT12. Peak inflammation coincided with enhanced STAT1/STAT3/STAT6 activation and altered core clock protein expression, supporting chronotherapeutic approaches for asthma.

papers.title: Polysomnographic and nocturnal heart rate correlates of cognitive impairment in Parkinson's disease: a cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: Cross-sectional study of 84 Parkinson's disease patients examining polysomnographic and nocturnal ECG correlates of cognitive impairment; found shorter REM sleep latency and higher mean/minimum nocturnal heart rate in dementia versus normal cognition. In multivariable regression, mean nocturnal heart rate remained negatively and REM sleep latency positively associated with MoCA scores.

papers.title: Non-Covalent Poly(ADP-ribose) Signaling Organizes a Circadian E3 Ligase Network in the Brain.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Integrating GTEx brain transcriptomics, GWAS Catalog associations, CIRCA phase annotations, and Human Protein Atlas single-cell data, this study characterized PAR-binding E3 ubiquitin ligases across neural tissues and found they occupy structured, non-random circadian windows with distinct co-phasing to BMAL1 and CRY1. The findings support a brain-deployed, circadian-organized PAR-binding E3 ligase regulatory layer enriched in microglia and linked to cognition, neurodegeneration, and sleep/circadian phenotypes.

papers.title: Sex- and gender-related differences in narcolepsy and idiopathic hypersomnia: a narrative review.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on sex- and gender-related differences across narcolepsy type 1, narcolepsy type 2, and idiopathic hypersomnia, reporting longer diagnostic delays in females with narcolepsy, greater subjective sleepiness and psychiatric comorbidity in females, and greater relationship impacts and suicidality in males. It highlights limited and inconsistent human mechanistic evidence and calls for prospective sex-stratified studies and objective biomarkers.

papers.title: Chrononutrition, Dietary Patterns, and Sleep: A Narrative Review of Current Evidence and Practical Implications.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence linking nutrients, foods, dietary patterns, chrononutrition, caffeine, and alcohol to sleep, finding that higher-quality Mediterranean-style diets are generally associated with more favorable sleep, while evidence for meal timing and time-restricted eating is inconsistent. Caffeine and alcohol have relatively well-established sleep-disrupting effects, and insufficient sleep alters dietary intake and metabolic health, supporting bidirectional nutrition-sleep relationships.

papers.title: Multimodal evidence associated with 20Hz rTMS in AD: neuroaxonal injury reduction, neural oscillatory rebalancing, and multilayer network integration.
papers.summary: A randomized sham-controlled trial in 16 patients with AD followed by a single-arm multimodal cohort of 30 patients found that DLPFC-targeted 20 Hz rTMS improved MMSE and MoCA scores, decreased NfL concentrations, reduced left temporal delta power, increased parietal beta and temporal gamma power, and reduced modularity with enhanced global efficiency. MoCA improvement correlated with gamma-band global efficiency and multilayer clustering coefficients.

papers.title: Temporal evolution of EEG hallmarks in childhood Lennox-Gastaut syndrome.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 51 children with Lennox-Gastaut syndrome, review of 234 sleep video-EEGs showed that slow spike-and-wave complexes emerged earlier than generalized paroxysmal fast activity (mean age 8.3 vs 9.6 years, p=0.002), with full electroclinical LGS criteria met at a median age of 10.9 years. These findings indicate a prolonged developmental phase between epilepsy onset and complete EEG expression of LGS.

papers.title: The Circadian Clock in Glioblastoma: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Potential.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence linking circadian rhythm disruption and altered core circadian gene expression to glioblastoma pathogenesis, and discusses chronotherapy—aligning chemotherapy and radiotherapy with patients' internal clocks—as a potential strategy to improve treatment efficacy. The authors conclude that further investigation is needed before circadian-based therapeutic approaches can be translated.

papers.title: Mapping Retinal Gene Expression to Cell Classes: Insights into Retinal Circadian Rhythms.
papers.summary: The authors present a mathematical model built on human retinal single-cell RNA sequencing data that assigns cell classes to over 10,000 genes with uniquely enriched expression, validated against known retinal markers. Applied to circadian-expressed genes from mouse ocular transcriptomic data, the model assigned cell classes to over 35% of genes and revealed significant enrichment of photoreceptor-associated transcripts linked to phototransduction and outer segment turnover.

papers.title: A melatonin textile transdermal patch based on physicochemical synergistic permeation-enhancement strategy for circadian rhythm regulation.
papers.summary: The authors developed a three-layer melatonin textile transdermal patch combining an electret backing with a permeation enhancer (optimally -1500 V electret plus 10% oleic acid) to achieve physicochemical synergistic permeation enhancement without disrupting the skin barrier. In vivo, the patch reached peak plasma melatonin (>30 ng/mL) within 1 h, maintained therapeutic levels (>5 ng/mL) for up to 8 h, and improved sleep quality in insomniac rats without skin irritation or cytotoxicity.

papers.title: Nanoscale remodeling of synaptic glutamate receptors and calcium channels in temporal lobe epilepsy
papers.summary: Using freeze-fracture replica immunolabeling of surgically resected human cortex, the study mapped nanoscale organization of AMPA receptors and presynaptic CaV2.1 channels in temporal lobe epilepsy versus non-epileptogenic tissue. AMPAR density increased at both spine and shaft synapses, with synapse-type-specific redistribution, while CaV2.1 density and nanocluster size/number increased predominantly at excitatory spine synapses.

papers.title: Recognizing fibromyalgia-like pain phenotypes in lipedema: A narrative review.
papers.summary: This SANRA-guided narrative review proposes a clinical framework for distinguishing characteristic lipedema tissue pain from musculoskeletal pain generators, secondary central pain amplification, and potentially coexisting fibromyalgia. It concludes that observational evidence cannot determine whether widespread pain in lipedema is intrinsic, secondary to biomechanical dysfunction or central sensitization, or an independent fibromyalgia comorbidity, and recommends multidisciplinary assessment including joint hypermobility and instability.

papers.title: Cofactors in Anaphylaxis: Insights From the European Anaphylaxis Registry.
papers.journal: Clinical and experimental allergy : journal of the British Society for Allergy and Clinical Immunology
papers.summary: Analysis of 16,915 cases in the European Anaphylaxis Registry (2007-2024) found at least one suspected cofactor in 49% of cases, with medication most common in adults (41%) and exercise in children (19%). Increasing number of suspected cofactors trended with greater reaction severity, and cofactors were associated with longer exposure-to-onset intervals in food-induced anaphylaxis.

papers.title: Parathyroid Storm Secondary to a Parathyroid Adenoma Presenting With Recurrent Generalised Tonic-Clonic Seizures and Refractory Hypercalcaemia: A Case Report.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 70-year-old woman with primary hyperparathyroidism presenting as parathyroid storm with severe hypercalcaemia (4.14 mmol/L), recurrent generalised tonic-clonic seizures, hypoventilation, and metabolic encephalopathy. Hypercalcaemia remained refractory to multimodal medical therapy but sustained calcium normalisation and seizure cessation followed urgent parathyroidectomy, with histopathology confirming a benign parathyroid adenoma.

papers.title: Interpreting Cytomegalovirus Seropositivity Beyond the Neonatal Diagnostic Window: A Case Report on an Infant With Early-Onset Atopic Dermatitis and Congenital Arthrogryposis.
papers.summary: This case report describes a six-month-old infant with a complex phenotype including microcephaly, early-onset atopic dermatitis, congenital arthrogryposis, growth impairment, and abnormal auditory and visual evoked potentials, with positive maternal and infant CMV serology but no virological confirmation within the first 21 days of life. Conventional dermatologic treatment reduced the SCORAD index from 45 to 18, and the report emphasises testing for congenital CMV within the neonatal diagnostic window.

papers.title: Creative patient and public engagement to amplify the voices of people living with eczema.
papers.summary: The "Surface Echoes" project used multidisciplinary creative patient and public engagement—collaging patient quotes into a read-aloud script and digital audio recording—to convey eczema experiences to broader audiences. The work was designed to raise awareness, reduce stigma, improve empathic discussion with professionals, and may inform future research.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
